cna.title: Beta9 build sandbox escape via chroot-only isolation

scenarios.value: Default clip v2 layered image build on a privileged build-pool worker

timeline.value: Fix merged in pull request 1897 (commit a28bf12)
Fixed release worker-0.1.756 published. No vendor security advisory was filed with the pull request.

solutions.value: Upgrade the Beta9 worker to 0.1.756 or later. That release drops chroot isolation: Buildah RUN steps use OCI isolation with private PID, IPC, and network namespaces, and tenant build arguments are applied inside the build container rather than in the Buildah process environment. The fix is commit a28bf12 (pull request 1897), released as worker-0.1.756 on 2026-09-15. Gateway 0.1.776 is the gateway tag cut from the same commit; the isolation change itself is in the worker image.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade the Beta9 worker to 0.1.756 or later. That release drops chroot isolation: Buildah RUN steps use OCI isolation with private PID, IPC, and network namespaces, and tenant build arguments are applied inside the build container rather than in the Buildah process environment. The fix is commit a28bf12 (pull request 1897), released as worker-0.1.756 on 2026-09-15. Gateway 0.1.776 is the gateway tag cut from the same commit; the isolation change itself is in the worker image.

references.name: Handle sandbox edge cases (fix pull request)

descriptions.value: Beta9 turns each shell command in a tenant image definition into a Dockerfile RUN line and executes it with Buildah on the build worker. The worker image sets BUILDAH_ISOLATION=chroot, and no buildah invocation passes --isolation, so the step only changes its filesystem root. It keeps the worker pod's PID, network, IPC, and user namespaces, runs as uid 0, and holds CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE. PID 1 in that procfs is the worker entrypoint, so /proc/1/root is the worker container's filesystem and is writable. That filesystem contains the runc, buildah, and runsc binaries the worker uses to start tenant containers, the worker's Kubernetes service account token, and the host directories mounted into the pod. Worker pods are privileged. Clip v2 layered builds are the default, so a tenant with a workspace token reaches this by submitting one image build. The read-only proof confirmed the shared namespaces, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, and that the worker's runc binary is visible at /proc/1/root. Fixed in worker 0.1.756: Buildah RUN steps, including the WORKDIR mkdir, use OCI isolation with private PID, IPC, and network namespaces, and tenant ARG values are passed only into the build container.

descriptions.value: Several psqlODBC entry points use an application-supplied column number or row index as an array index without validating it. SQLBindCol with a column number above 32767 wraps the binding count negative and a later copy runs off the array. A negative SQL_DESC_COUNT on an application row descriptor unbinds columns at negative indexes. SQLColAttribute with a very large column number uses a negative index. SQLSetPos(SQL_ADD) does not check the row number against the rowset size. An application that forwards untrusted column or row numbers exposes its process to out-of-bounds reads and writes. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

cna.title: Beta9 container escape via unvalidated sandbox file paths

scenarios.value: Tenant with a workspace token and a running sandbox on a worker that serves the sandbox file API

timeline.value: Fix merged in pull request 1897 (commit a28bf12)
Fixed release worker-0.1.756 published. No vendor security advisory was filed with the pull request.

solutions.value: Upgrade the Beta9 worker to 0.1.756 or later. Sandbox file APIs and workspace sync use os.OpenRoot, so parent-directory segments and symbolic links stay inside the container root or the mount source. File operations refuse read-only mounts and do not write through a symlink swapped in after path resolution. The fix is commit a28bf12 (pull request 1897), released as worker-0.1.756 on 2026-09-15.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade the Beta9 worker to 0.1.756 or later. Sandbox file APIs and workspace sync use os.OpenRoot, so parent-directory segments and symbolic links stay inside the container root or the mount source. references.name: Handle sandbox edge cases (fix pull request)

descriptions.value: The Beta9 worker serves the sandbox file API from outside the container. getHostPathFromContainerPath turns the tenant's container path into a worker path. If the unresolved path starts with a mount destination, including the default upload mount at /tmp/.beta9, the remainder is joined onto that mount's source with filepath.Join, which cleans parent-directory segments after the prefix check. A long enough run of those segments names any absolute path on the worker. A path that matches no mount is joined onto the container root and opened in the worker's own filesystem, so an absolute symbolic link such as /var/run pointing at /run is followed against the worker root. Upload, download, stat, list, find-in-files, replace-in-files, and delete-file all call this helper. A tenant with a workspace token and one running sandbox can read, write, list, and delete files on the hosting worker as root, including files of other tenants on that machine. A read-only proof downloaded the worker pod's Kubernetes service account token through the file API for a path that did not exist inside the sandbox. In the shipped remote-node manifests that service account is bound to cluster-admin. Fixed in worker 0.1.756: sandbox file operations and workspace sync open paths with os.OpenRoot, so parent-directory and symlink lookups stay inside the container root or the mount source.

cna.title: psqlODBC stack buffer overflow copying ctid and oid values for updatable cursors

solutions.value: Upgrade to psqlODBC 18.00.0006 or later. The driver rejects a keyset value that does not fit its buffer, and the query fails with SQLSTATE HY000.

workarounds.value: Set UpdatableCursors=0 in the connection string or DSN, so the driver does not add the keyset columns.

descriptions.value: For updatable cursors, which are enabled by default, psqlODBC adds hidden ctid and, for tables with OIDs, oid columns to the query. It copies each value into a 32-byte stack buffer using the length the server sent, without checking it against the buffer size, so a value of 32 bytes or more writes past the buffer. A server not trusted under current SSL settings can send such a value. So can any database user who can create a view with its own column named ctid that the application reads with an updatable cursor. Builds with _FORTIFY_SOURCE abort; other builds overwrite adjacent stack memory. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

affected.product: SureCart – Ecommerce Made Easy For Selling Physical Products, Digital Downloads, Subscriptions, Donations, & Payments

descriptions.value: The SureCart plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthenticated account takeover in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.5. The passwordless one-time-code login REST route (VerificationCodeController::verify(), whose permission callback returns true) resolves an attacker-supplied login to any WordPress user, verifies a 6-digit code, and on success calls $user->login() → wp_set_auth_cookie() for a user of any role. In the affected versions this path has no per-account attempt counter, no persistent email/IP lockout or rate limit (the upstream CDN throttle is bypassable via IP rotation), and no restriction preventing high-privilege accounts from being logged in through it. An unauthenticated attacker can trigger a code for any user (including an administrator) via the companion unauthenticated endpoint and brute-force the 6-digit code to obtain an authenticated session as that user, resulting in a full administrator account takeover.

cna.title: psqlODBC ODBC escape parser stack buffer overflow

solutions.value: Upgrade to psqlODBC 18.00.0006 or later. The argument offset array is initialized and bounded, and the escape body copy reserves room for the terminator.

workarounds.value: Do not pass SQL text from untrusted sources to the driver, or reject text containing ODBC escape sequences ({fn ...}, {d ...}, {t ...}, {ts ...}, {escape ...}) before it reaches the driver.

descriptions.value: The psqlODBC parser for ODBC escape sequences in application SQL text writes the argument offsets of a {fn} escape into a fixed 16-entry stack array without a bound and does not initialize the array. An escape with too many arguments overflows the stack, and a reference to an unsupplied argument copies arbitrary bytes into the query. The copy of a {d}, {t}, {ts}, or {escape} body also writes one byte past a 128-byte stack buffer. An application that forwards untrusted SQL text to the driver exposes its process to memory corruption. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

cna.title: Silent element-count truncation via 32-bit bit-length overflow in packed-bit vector views

descriptions.value: A weakness in the BSON library's handling of a specialized binary vector data type allows an arithmetic wraparound when computing the number of elements described by an oversized attacker-supplied value. On builds where the platform word size is 32 bits, an application that parses untrusted BSON data can be made to process only a small fraction of the supplied elements while the operation reports success, producing results that disagree with byte-oriented accessors and with 64-bit builds of the same library. No authentication or user interaction is required beyond getting the application to parse the data. The impact is limited to data integrity; memory safety is not affected and no information is disclosed.

cna.title: fastify vulnerable to Denial of Service via uncaught exception on handlerTimeout with streaming responses

descriptions.value: fastify is a web framework for Node.js. In versions 5.8.0 through 5.12.7, when the server is configured with a nonzero handlerTimeout and a route returns a streaming response, a request whose stream has already sent its headers but stays open past the timeout crashes the server. When the timeout fires, Fastify tries to send a new error response on a response that has already started, raising an uncaught ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT that terminates the Node.js process and interrupts any other in-flight requests. An unauthenticated remote client can trigger this with a single request to an affected streaming endpoint, so the impact is availability only, and exploitation requires the non-default handlerTimeout to be set. The default handlerTimeout of 0 is not affected. The issue is fixed in fastify 5.12.8, and users should upgrade to 5.12.8 or later. As a workaround, set handlerTimeout to 0, which disables the affected timeout path.

The default handlerTimeout of 0 is not affected. The issue is fixed in fastify 5.12.8, and users should upgrade to 5.12.8 or later. As a workaround, set handlerTimeout to 0, which disables the affected timeout path.

cna.title: @fastify/http-proxy vulnerable to prefix escape via percent-encoded backslash dot-segments

descriptions.value: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP requests to an upstream server under a configured prefix. In versions 11.6.0 through 11.6.2, the destination validation normalizes literal backslashes before it percent-decodes the request path, so a path that encodes its backslashes and dot-segments survives the dot-segment check and is only turned into backslash and double-dot sequences after that check has passed. When the upstream resolves on a platform that treats a backslash as a path separator, the forwarded request walks out of the configured proxy prefix and reaches a sibling location on the upstream. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use this to retrieve upstream resources outside the intended prefix, so the impact is confidentiality only, and exploitation depends on the upstream's path handling. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.3, and users should upgrade to 11.6.3 or later. This is a follow-up to the earlier prefix-escape fix, which did not account for the encoded-backslash form.

cna.title: @fastify/http-proxy vulnerable to prefix escape via decoded route parameters

descriptions.value: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP requests to an upstream server under a configured prefix. In versions 9.0.0 through 11.6.5, when an application uses parameterized prefix and rewritePrefix options to pin clients to a fixed upstream path, the plugin substitutes URL-decoded route parameters into rewritePrefix without re-encoding them. A parameter value that encodes a path separator together with a fragment or query delimiter therefore decodes into real separators and delimiters that inject extra upstream path segments and strip the mandatory suffix the rewritePrefix was meant to enforce, without using any dot-dot traversal. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use this to reach upstream locations outside the intended prefix, leading to path-restriction bypass and, depending on the upstream, server-side request forgery or authorization bypass in the proxied service. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.6, and users should upgrade to 11.6.6 or later. There is no workaround other than upgrading.

cna.title: Uncontrolled Recursion in HDF5 H5B__iterate_helper() via Crafted File

descriptions.value: HDF5 through 2.2.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in H5B__iterate_helper() in src/H5B.c. When iterating a version 1 B-tree, the function does not verify that a child node’s level matches the expected level. That check is performed only in H5B__cache_deserialize() when a node is first loaded into the metadata cache. A crafted HDF5 file whose B-tree child pointer refers back to a node already in the cache, such as a node that points to itself, bypasses the check and causes unbounded recursion, leading to stack exhaustion and a crash. This can be triggered by calling H5Gget_info() or H5Gget_num_objs() on a group in the crafted file, which reaches H5B_iterate() through H5G__obj_info() and H5G__stab_count(). An attacker who can get a user or application to open a malicious file can cause a denial of service.

An attacker who can get a user or application to open a malicious file can cause a denial of service.

cna.title: Prefab UI Pyodide sandbox escape to host RCE

scenarios.value: FastMCP server with GenerativeUI enabled, Deno installed, and no authentication configured
Authenticated client allowed to call tools on a server that executes untrusted code in the Generative UI sandbox

timeline.value: Pyodide sandbox added with --allow-read, --allow-write, and --allow-net (commit fc4362f3, pull request 334)
prefab-ui 0.14.0 published on PyPI, the first release that includes the sandbox
prefab-ui 0.20.2 published. This is the release confirmed in testing.
Reported to PrefectHQ as GHSA-595q-jv4r-q7j9. The advisory is still in triage and has no CVE id.
Fix merged in pull request 538 (commit 030f074). The runner revokes read, write, and network permission before accepting code.
prefab-ui 0.21.0 published on PyPI with the fix. No vendor advisory text was published with the release.

references.name: Refresh dependencies and fix renderer and sandbox regressions (fix pull request)

descriptions.value: Prefab UI's Generative UI sandbox runs caller-supplied Python inside Pyodide, Python compiled to WebAssembly, in a Deno subprocess. The feature is documented as isolation for untrusted code, including LLM-written UI. From prefab-ui 0.14.0 through 0.20.2 the launcher starts Deno with unrestricted --allow-read, --allow-write, and --allow-net, and the runner leaves the Deno API on the JavaScript global object. Pyodide's js module proxies that global, so the Python can call Deno.readTextFileSync and Deno.writeTextFileSync. A caller who can supply the code can read and write files as the server OS user, and can persist code execution by writing a .pth file into the server virtualenv's site-packages. The usual remote path is FastMCP's GenerativeUI provider, which registers the MCP tool generate_prefab_ui and forwards that tool's code argument into this sandbox. On a FastMCP server with no authentication configured, any client who can reach the server can call the tool. With authentication, any client allowed to call tools can. Generative UI is opt-in, and the host must have Deno installed. Confirmed on prefab-ui 0.20.2. Fixed in 0.21.0: after the runtime and Prefab sources load, the runner revokes Deno read, write, and network permission before it accepts code, the process is started with --no-prompt so a permission request cannot grant them again, and bootstrap network access is limited to cdn.jsdelivr.net. The fix is commit 030f074 (pull request 538).

cna.title: Libslirp: libslirp: queue pointer corruption in if_output() leading to denial of service

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Piyusha Akash (Manifold Operations) for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Red Hat is not aware of a practical temporary workaround that fully mitigates this issue or meets Red Hat Product Security's standards for usability, deployment, applicability, or stability. Customers are advised to apply the relevant security updates when/if they become available.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in libslirp in if_output(). When moving a session from the fast queue to the batch queue, the code unlinked and reinserted an arbitrary packet via ifm->m_nextpkt instead of the session queue head, corrupting queue pointers. A guest generating burst traffic could crash the host networking process, causing a denial of service.

cna.title: psqlODBC uses a server-supplied column name as a format string

solutions.value: Upgrade to psqlODBC 18.00.0006 or later. Each percent sign in the server-supplied column name is doubled before the name is placed in the format string.

workarounds.value: Set UpdatableCursors=0 in the connection string or DSN, or use read-only cursors (SQL_CONCUR_READ_ONLY).

descriptions.value: For an updatable cursor over a table without OIDs that has an auto-increment int4 column, psqlODBC places that column's name, as reported by the server, into a printf-style format string. It later expands that string with one argument while it builds the WHERE clause of its positioned SELECT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements. A column name that contains format directives makes the driver read unrelated memory, which can crash the application or copy client memory into query text sent to the server. The name can come from a server not trusted under current SSL settings, or from any database user who can create a table that the application reads with an updatable cursor. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

cna.title: Reflected XSS via client window id in URL client window mode

descriptions.value: CAPEC-591 Reflected XSS

In Eclipse Mojarra versions 2.2.0 through 4.0.28, 4.1.0 through 4.1.19, and 5.0.0-M1 through 5.0.0-M11, when URL client window mode is enabled (`jakarta.faces.CLIENT_WINDOW_MODE=url`), the client window id from the `jfwid` or `jakarta.faces.ClientWindow` request parameter is appended to generated URLs without URL-encoding. `h:button` renders such a URL into a JavaScript string literal, which allows reflected cross-site scripting. cna.title: psqlODBC large-object read overflows the application buffer

solutions.value: Upgrade to psqlODBC 18.00.0006 or later. CC_send_function receives the caller's buffer size, clamps the copy to it, and rejects short fixed-size replies.

workarounds.value: Do not fetch large-object (lo) columns from servers that are not authenticated with sslmode=verify-full or an equivalent GSS setting.

descriptions.value: psqlODBC copies the reply to a large-object read (loread) into the application's buffer using the length sent by the server, without comparing it to the buffer size. A server not trusted under current SSL settings, or a man-in-the-middle, can return more bytes than the buffer holds and overwrite adjacent memory in the client process with server-chosen bytes. Fetching any large-object column is sufficient to trigger it. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

This is possible because an operator-precedence bug in handle_scripts() causes the admin bundle — and its inlined nekit-admin-nonce — to be enqueued on every admin screen accessible to Subscribers (such as /wp-admin/profile.php), and because sanitize_text_field() is applied to the raw JSON string before json_decode(), allowing angle brackets encoded as \u003c/\u003e to survive sanitization and be restored to literal angle brackets, enabling overwrite of _elementor_data on any post.

cna.title: psqlODBC log files are created with default permissions at a predictable path and follow symbolic links

solutions.value: Upgrade to psqlODBC 18.00.0006 or later. On Unix-like systems, log files are opened with mode 0600 and O_NOFOLLOW, and an existing log file is used only if it is a regular file owned by the user running the application.

workarounds.value: Leave Debug and CommLog disabled in production. If logging is needed, set Logdir in the driver's section of odbcinst.ini (PostgreSQL Unicode or PostgreSQL ANSI) to a directory writable only by the user running the application.

descriptions.value: On Unix-like systems, when logging is enabled, psqlODBC creates its log files in /tmp by default, named from the program name, user name, and process ID, with the default permissions, typically world-readable, and follows symbolic links when opening them. A local user can read query text and data from another user's logs, and can place a symbolic link at the predictable path so that the driver appends log data to a file of the attacker's choosing with the victim's privileges. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

solutions.value:
*  PR:  https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/pull/841 https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/pull/841

supportingMedia.value:
• PR: https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/pull/841

descriptions.value:
Summary

A Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability was discovered in the AI Playground's OAuth callback handler. The `error_description` query parameter was directly interpolated into an HTML script tag without proper escaping, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the victim's session.




Root cause

The OAuth callback handler in `site/ai-playground/src/server.ts` directly interpolated the `authError` value, sourced from the `error_description` query parameter,  into an inline `<script>` tag.


Impact

An attacker could craft a malicious link that, when clicked by a victim, would:

  *  Steal user chat message history - Access all LLM interactions stored in the user's session.


  *  Access connected MCP Servers - Interact with any MCP servers connected to the victim's session (public or authenticated/private), potentially allowing the attacker to perform actions on the victim's behalf





Mitigation:

  *  PR:  https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/pull/841 https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/pull/841 




  *  Agents-sdk users should upgrade to agents@0.3.10




  *  Developers using configureOAuthCallback with custom error handling in their own applications should ensure all user-controlled input is escaped before interpolation.

  1. Steal user chat message history - Access all LLM interactions stored in the user's session.

  2. Access connected MCP Servers - Interact with any MCP servers connected to the victim's session (public or authenticated/private), potentially allowing the attacker to perform actions on the victim's behalf


Mitigation:

cna.title: Auth misconfiguration when multiple providers enabled

descriptions.value: CAPEC-180 Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels

An edgecase in SSO implementation in Neo4j Enterprise edition versions prior to version 2026.02 can lead to unauthorised access under the following conditions:


If a neo4j admin configures two or more OIDC providers AND configures one or more of them to be an authorization provider AND configures one or more of them to be authentication-only, then those that are authentication-only will also provide authorization. This edgecase becomes a security problem only if the authentication-only provider contains groups which have higher privileges than provided by the intended (configured) authorization provider.  

When using multiple plugins for authentication and authorisation, prior to the fix the issue could lead to a plugin configured to provide only authentication or authorisation capabilities erroneously providing both capabilities. 

We recommend upgrading to versions 2026.02 (or 5.26.22) where the issue is fixed.

solutions.value:
Harden the configuration
Who should apply this recommendation: All users


To reduce the risk of exploitation, ARC Informatique strongly recommends implementing the following defensive measures:

  *  Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, and ensure they are not accessible from insecure networks.
  *  Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolate them from business networks.
  *  When remote access is required, use secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as its connected devices.



Uninstall the Web Server 
Who should apply this recommendation: All users not using the affected component 

If your system does not require the use of the Web & Mobile features, you should make sure not to install them. If your system requires the use of the Web & Mobile features, they should be installed only on the Web Server.
See the product help related to the installation for more information.


Update the Web Deployment Console (WDC) and re deploy the Web Server
Who should apply this recommendation: 

All users running affected components.



Install a patched release of the Web Deployment Console (WDC) on the IIS Web server and use it to re-deploy the Web Site. Some settings might need to be updated if third-party web apps or services depend on the OAuth ROPC flow.

In a patched release of the WDC, new settings are available for each authorized Client to enable or disable:
  *  The Authorization Code flow
  *  The Authorization Code flow with PKCE
  *  The Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC) flow


By default, all the OAuth flows are now disabled for third-party web apps and need to be manually enabled before deployment if required.

To verify that the patch is applied correctly, you must check that:
  *  The File version property of the file ./bin/Modules/WebDeployment/WebDeploymentConsole.exe matches the deployed release or later, and ensure that any earlier release is no longer used;
  *  Web Sites have been redeployed;
  *  OAuth flow are correctly set for each authorized Client.





Available patches:
Patch provided in:
  *  PcVue 16.3.4 (16.3.4902.3112)
  *  PcVue 15.2.14 (15.2.14900.37147)

cna.title: Missing security HTTP headers

exploits.value: No POC available.

supportingMedia.value: No POC available.

exploits.value: Not known to be exploited

supportingMedia.value: Not known to be exploited

solutions.value:
Harden the configuration
Who should apply this recommendation: All users


To reduce the risk of exploitation, ARC Informatique strongly recommends implementing the following defensive measures:

  *  Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, and ensure they are not accessible from insecure networks.
  *  Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolate them from business networks.
  *  When remote access is required, use secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as its connected devices.



Uninstall the Web Server 
Who should apply this recommendation: All users not using the affected component 

If your system does not require the use of the Web & Mobile features, you should make sure not to install them. If your system requires the use of the Web & Mobile features, they should be installed only on the Web Server.
See the product help related to the installation for more information.




Update IIS configuration – manually update HTTP headers
Who should apply this recommendation: 

All users running affected components.



As a quick mitigation for the unnecessary and missing HTTP headers, you can disable default headers and add secure HTTP headers for all requests. Those options can be set via the web.config file located on the IIS by following those steps:
  *  Open the file C:\inetpub\<SV Website>\web.config
  *  Add the following entries to the section customHeaders, which are the recommendations from the official OWASP site:
<remove name="X-Powered-By" />
<add name="X-Frame-Options" value="DENY" />
<add name="X-XSS-Protection" value="0" />
<add name="X-Content-Type-Options" value="nosniff" />
<add name="X-DNS-Prefetch-Control" value="off" />
<add name="Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy" value="same-origin" />
<add name="Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy" value="require-corp" />
<add name="Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy" value="same-site" />
<add name="Referrer-Policy" value="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" />
<add name="Strict-Transport-Security" value="max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload" />
<add name="Permissions-Policy" value="geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()" />




Update the Web Deployment Console (WDC) and re deploy the Web Server
Who should apply this recommendation: 

All users running affected components.



Install a patched release of the Web Deployment Console (WDC) on the IIS Web server and use it to re-deploy the Web Site. Some settings might need to be updated if third-party web apps or services depend on the OAuth ROPC flow.

In a patched release of the WDC, new settings are available for each authorized Client to enable or disable:
  *  The Authorization Code flow
  *  The Authorization Code flow with PKCE
  *  The Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC) flow


By default, all the OAuth flows are now disabled for third-party web apps and need to be manually enabled before deployment if required.

To verify that the patch is applied correctly, you must check that:
  *  The File version property of the file ./bin/Modules/WebDeployment/WebDeploymentConsole.exe matches the deployed release or later, and ensure that any earlier release is no longer used;
  *  Web Sites have been redeployed;
  *  OAuth flow are correctly set for each authorized Client.





Available patches:
Patch provided in:
  *  PcVue 16.3.4 (16.3.4902.3112)
  *  PcVue 15.2.14 (15.2.14900.37147)

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in org.eclipse.jetty. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending a compressed HTTP request with Content-Encoding: gzip when the server's response is not compressed. This prevents the release of the JDK Inflater, leading to a resource leak. This resource exhaustion can result in a Denial of Service (DoS), making the server unavailable to legitimate users.

descriptions.description: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime

descriptions.value:
In Eclipse Jetty, versions 12.0.0-12.0.31 and 12.1.0-12.0.5, class GzipHandler exposes a vulnerability when a compressed HTTP request, with Content-Encoding: gzip, is processed and the corresponding response is not compressed.


This happens because the JDK Inflater is allocated for decompressing the request, but it is not released because the release mechanism is tied to the compressed response.
In this case, since the response is not compressed, the release mechanism does not trigger, causing the leak.

supportingMedia.value:
In Eclipse Jetty, versions 12.0.0-12.0.31 and 12.1.0-12.0.5, class GzipHandler exposes a vulnerability when a compressed HTTP request, with Content-Encoding: gzip, is processed and the corresponding response is not compressed.

This happens because the JDK Inflater is allocated for decompressing the request, but it is not released because the release mechanism is tied to the compressed response. In this case, since the response is not compressed, the release mechanism does not trigger, causing the leak.

descriptions.description: CWE-401 Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

cna.title: Information Disclosure via Bucket Squatting in Google Cloud Agentspace.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-131 Resource Leak Exposure

The Agentspace service was affected by a vulnerability that exposed sensitive information due to the use of predictable Google Cloud Storage bucket names. These names were utilized for error logs and temporary staging during data imports from GCS and Cloud SQL. This predictability allowed an attacker to engage in "bucket squatting" by establishing these buckets before a victim's initial use.

All versions after December 12th, 2025 have been updated to protect from this vulnerability. No user action is required for this.

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Codean Labs for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: To mitigate this issue, avoid processing untrusted URLs in applications that use the libsoup library with an HTTP proxy configured. Restricting network access to the HTTP proxy can also limit potential exposure.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in libsoup, an HTTP client library. This vulnerability, known as CRLF (Carriage Return Line Feed) Injection, occurs when an HTTP proxy is configured and the library improperly handles URL-decoded input used to create the Host header. A remote attacker can exploit this by providing a specially crafted URL containing CRLF sequences, allowing them to inject additional HTTP headers or complete HTTP request bodies. This can lead to unintended or unauthorized HTTP requests being forwarded by the proxy, potentially impacting downstream services.

descriptions.value: The WPGSI: Spreadsheet Integration plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized modification and loss of data due to missing capability checks and an insecure authentication mechanism on the `wpgsi_callBackFuncAccept` and `wpgsi_callBackFuncUpdate` REST API functions in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.3. Both REST endpoints use `permission_callback => '__return_true'`, allowing unauthenticated access. The plugin's custom token-based validation relies on a Base64-encoded JSON object containing the user ID and email address, but is not cryptographically signed. cna.title: Migration, Backup, Staging <= 0.9.123 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload

affected.product: Migration, Backup, Staging – WPvivid Backup & Migration

descriptions.value: The Migration, Backup, Staging – WPvivid Backup & Migration plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload in versions up to and including 0.9.123. This is due to improper error handling in the RSA decryption process combined with a lack of path sanitization when writing uploaded files. When the plugin fails to decrypt a session key using openssl_private_decrypt(), it does not terminate execution and instead passes the boolean false value to the phpseclib library's AES cipher initialization. The library treats this false value as a string of null bytes, allowing an attacker to encrypt a malicious payload using a predictable null-byte key. Additionally, the plugin accepts filenames from the decrypted payload without sanitization, enabling directory traversal to escape the protected backup directory. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload arbitrary PHP files to publicly accessible directories and achieve Remote Code Execution via the wpvivid_action=send_to_site parameter.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the libsoup HTTP library that can cause proxy authentication credentials to be sent to unintended destinations. When handling HTTP redirects, libsoup removes the Authorization header but does not remove the Proxy-Authorization header if the request is redirected to a different host. As a result, sensitive proxy credentials may be leaked to third-party servers. Applications using libsoup for HTTP communication may unintentionally expose proxy authentication data.

cna.title: Restore restriction bypass via key disclosure vulnerability (pgAdmin 4)

descriptions.value: pgAdmin versions 9.11 are affected by a Restore restriction bypass via key disclosure vulnerability that occurs when running in server mode and performing restores from PLAIN-format dump files. An attacker with access to the pgAdmin web interface can observe an active restore operation, extract the `\restrict` key in real time, and race the restore process by overwriting the restore script with a payload that re-enables meta-commands using `\unrestrict <key>`. This results in reliable command execution on the pgAdmin host during the restore operation.

cna.title: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in django.utils.text.Truncator HTML methods

descriptions.value: CAPEC-130: Excessive Allocation

An issue was discovered in 6.0 before 6.0.2, 5.2 before 5.2.11, and 4.2 before 4.2.28.
`django.utils.text.Truncator.chars()` and `Truncator.words()` methods (with `html=True`) and the `truncatechars_html` and `truncatewords_html` template filters allow a remote attacker to cause a potential denial-of-service via crafted inputs containing a large number of unmatched HTML end tags.
Earlier, unsupported Django series (such as 5.0.x, 4.1.x, and 3.2.x) were not evaluated and may also be affected.
Django would like to thank Seokchan Yoon for reporting this issue.

cna.title: Libxml2: memory leak leading to local denial of service in xmllint interactive shell

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank lanbigking for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

descriptions.value: A flaw was identified in the interactive shell of the xmllint utility, part of the libxml2 project, where memory allocated for user input is not properly released under certain conditions. When a user submits input consisting only of whitespace, the program skips command execution but fails to free the allocated buffer. Repeating this action causes memory to continuously accumulate. Over time, this can exhaust system memory and terminate the xmllint process, creating a denial-of-service condition on the local system.

descriptions.description: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

workarounds.value:
Administrators can mitigate this issue by ensuring users who access a read only = yes Samba share do not have filesystem-level write permission to the exported files.

A server administrator may also monitor and remove unintended "user.SmbReparse" xattr (extended attributes) and the associated FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT "user.DosAttrib" bit metadata if exploitation is suspected.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in Samba’s handling of NTFS-style reparse points on shares configured with read only = yes. Due to missing SMB-layer access checks, authenticated users with underlying filesystem write permissions may create or delete reparse point metadata through SMB operations even on read-only exports. This could allow modification of SMB-visible file behavior, including converting files into symbolic links or other reparse point types.

solutions.value:
Labkotec reports that it is not possible to implement secure and encrypted network traffic on the LID-3300IP. For this reason, Labkotec recommends updating ice detectors to the LID-3300IP Type 2 model and installing the latest firmware version V2.40. It is also highly recommended to activate HTTPS for network traffic. The device type and software version can be verified in the web interface.

Devices not connected to an Ethernet network are not susceptible to this attack. Ice detectors operating on secure internal networks that adhere to modern security standards, where only authorized devices and users have access, are protected against external threats.

Labkotec recommends implementing the following additional security controls:
* Do not connect the device to the public Internet
* Follow good security practices
* Change Default Credentials
* Enable Secure Management Access
* Network Segmentation
* Implement Firewall and Access Controls
* Restrict Protocols
* Monitor and Alert
* Avoid Direct Internet Exposure
* Keep Firmware Updated
* Control Physical Access
* Maintain Inventory and Access Reviews

Users can find more information in Labkotec's security advisory ( https://labkotec.fi/wp-content/uploads/CA-000001-Cybersecurity-Advisory.pdf) .

affected.product: ExactMetrics – Google Analytics Dashboard for WordPress (Website Stats Plugin)

descriptions.value: The ExactMetrics – Google Analytics Dashboard for WordPress plugin is vulnerable to Improper Privilege Management in versions 7.1.0 through 9.0.2. This is due to the `update_settings()` function accepting arbitrary plugin setting names without a whitelist of allowed settings. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with the `exactmetrics_save_settings` capability to modify any plugin setting, including the `save_settings` option that controls which user roles have access to plugin functionality. The admin intended to delegate configuration access to a trusted user, not enable that user to delegate access to everyone. By setting `save_settings` to include `subscriber`, an attacker can grant plugin administrative access to all subscribers on the site.

solutions.value:
Harden the configuration
Who should apply this recommendation: All users


To reduce the risk of exploitation, ARC Informatique strongly recommends implementing the following defensive measures:

  *  Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, and ensure they are not accessible from insecure networks.
  *  Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolate them from business networks.
  *  When remote access is required, use secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as its connected devices.



Uninstall the Web Server 
Who should apply this recommendation: All users not using the affected component 

If your system does not require the use of the Web & Mobile features, you should make sure not to install them. If your system requires the use of the Web & Mobile features, they should be installed only on the Web Server.
See the product help related to the installation for more information.


Update the Web Deployment Console (WDC) and re deploy the Web Server
Who should apply this recommendation: 

All users running affected components.



Install a patched release of the Web Deployment Console (WDC) on the IIS Web server and use it to re-deploy the Web Site. Some settings might need to be updated if third-party web apps or services depend on the OAuth ROPC flow.

In a patched release of the WDC, new settings are available for each authorized Client to enable or disable:
  *  The Authorization Code flow
  *  The Authorization Code flow with PKCE
  *  The Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC) flow


By default, all the OAuth flows are now disabled for third-party web apps and need to be manually enabled before deployment if required.

To verify that the patch is applied correctly, you must check that:
  *  The File version property of the file ./bin/Modules/WebDeployment/WebDeploymentConsole.exe matches the deployed release or later, and ensure that any earlier release is no longer used;
  *  Web Sites have been redeployed;
  *  OAuth flow are correctly set for each authorized Client.





Available patches:
Patch provided in:
  *  PcVue 16.3.4 (16.3.4902.3112)
  *  PcVue 15.2.14 (15.2.14900.37147)

cna.title: undici is vulnerable to CRLF Injection via upgrade option

supportingMedia.value:
Impact

When an application passes user-controlled input to the upgrade option of client.request(), an attacker can inject CRLF sequences (\r\n) to:

  1. Inject arbitrary HTTP headers
  2. Terminate the HTTP request prematurely and smuggle raw data to non-HTTP services (Redis, Memcached, Elasticsearch)

The vulnerability exists because undici writes the upgrade value directly to the socket without validating for invalid header characters:

// lib/dispatcher/client-h1.js:1121
if (upgrade) {
  header += `connection: upgrade\r\nupgrade: ${upgrade}\r\n`
}

descriptions.description: CWE-93 Improper neutralization of CRLF sequences ('CRLF injection')

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Ahmed Lekssays for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options don't meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base or stability.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in libsoup, an HTTP client/server library. This HTTP Request Smuggling vulnerability arises from non-RFC-compliant parsing in the soup_filter_input_stream_read_line() logic, where libsoup accepts malformed chunk headers, such as lone line feed (LF) characters instead of the required carriage return and line feed (CRLF). A remote attacker can exploit this without authentication or user interaction by sending specially crafted chunked requests. This allows libsoup to parse and process multiple HTTP requests from a single network message, potentially leading to information disclosure.

descriptions.description: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling')

cna.title: Command Injection in nvm via NVM_AUTH_HEADER in wget code path

descriptions.value: CAPEC-88 OS Command Injection
CAPEC-6 Argument Injection

solutions.value: Upgrade to nvm version 0.40.4 or later, which sanitizes NVM_AUTH_HEADER in the wget code path using nvm_sanitize_auth_header().

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to nvm version 0.40.4 or later, which sanitizes NVM_AUTH_HEADER in the wget code path using nvm_sanitize_auth_header().

descriptions.value: A command injection vulnerability exists in nvm (Node Version Manager) versions 0.40.3 and below. The nvm_download() function uses eval to execute wget commands, and the NVM_AUTH_HEADER environment variable was not sanitized in the wget code path (though it was sanitized in the curl code path). An attacker who can set environment variables in a victim's shell environment (e.g., via malicious CI/CD configurations, compromised dotfiles, or Docker images) can inject arbitrary shell commands that execute when the victim runs nvm commands that trigger downloads, such as 'nvm install' or 'nvm ls-remote'.

workarounds.value: To mitigate this issue, ensure that a Certificate Authority (CA) certificate is explicitly configured when setting up the connection to OpenShift in foreman_kubevirt. This will enable SSL verification and prevent Man-in-the-Middle attacks. Refer to the foreman_kubevirt documentation for specific instructions on configuring CA certificates. A restart or service reload may be required for the changes to take effect.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in foreman_kubevirt. When configuring the connection to OpenShift, the system disables SSL verification if a Certificate Authority (CA) certificate is not explicitly set. This insecure default allows a remote attacker, capable of intercepting network traffic between Satellite and OpenShift, to perform a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack. Such an attack could lead to the disclosure or alteration of sensitive information.

TP-Link Tapo C200 v5 contains a stack-based buffer overflow flaw in RTSP authentication handling due to improper validation of Authorization header field lengths, which can be triggered by a crafted authentication request.

cna.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) via Header-Based Email Routing

descriptions.value:
Summary

An Insecure Direct Object Reference has been found to exist in `createHeaderBasedEmailResolver()` function within the Cloudflare Agents SDK. The issue occurs because the `Message-ID` and `References` headers are parsed to derive the target agentName and agentId without proper validation or origin checks, allowing an external attacker with control of these headers to route inbound mail to arbitrary Durable Object instances and namespaces .




Root cause

The `createHeaderBasedEmailResolver()` function lacks cryptographic verification or origin validation for the headers used in the routing logic, effectively allowing external input to dictate internal object routing.




Impact

Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in email routing lets an attacker steer inbound mail to arbitrary Agent instances via spoofed Message-ID.





Mitigation:

  *  PR:  https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/main/docs/email.md ] provides the necessary architectural context for coding agents to mitigate the issue by refactoring the resolver to enforce strict identity boundaries.
  *  Agents-sdk users should  upgrade to agents@0.3.7

Mitigation:

cna.title: Incorrect Authorization vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed unauthorized merging of pull requests

descriptions.value: CAPEC-233 Privilege Escalation

An incorrect authorization vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an attacker to merge their own pull request into a repository without having push access by exploiting an authorization bypass in the enable_auto_merge mutation for pull requests. This issue only affected repositories that allow forking as the attack relies on opening a pull request from an attacker-controlled fork into the target repository. Exploitation was only possible in specific scenarios. It required a clean pull request status and only applied to branches without branch protection rules enabled. This vulnerability affected GitHub Enterprise Server versions prior to 3.19.2, 3.18.5, and 3.17.11, and was fixed in versions 3.19.2, 3.18.5, and 3.17.11. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

solutions.value:
Harden the configuration
Who should apply this recommendation: All users


To reduce the risk of exploitation, ARC Informatique strongly recommends implementing the following defensive measures:

  *  Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, and ensure they are not accessible from insecure networks.
  *  Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolate them from business networks.
  *  When remote access is required, use secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as its connected devices.



Uninstall the Web Server 
Who should apply this recommendation: All users not using the affected component 

If your system does not require the use of the Web & Mobile features, you should make sure not to install them. If your system requires the use of the Web & Mobile features, they should be installed only on the Web Server.
See the product help related to the installation for more information.


Update the Web Deployment Console (WDC) and re deploy the Web Server
Who should apply this recommendation: 

All users running affected components.



Install a patched release of the Web Deployment Console (WDC) on the IIS Web server and use it to re-deploy the Web Site. Some settings might need to be updated if third-party web apps or services depend on the OAuth ROPC flow.

In a patched release of the WDC, new settings are available for each authorized Client to enable or disable:
  *  The Authorization Code flow
  *  The Authorization Code flow with PKCE
  *  The Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC) flow


By default, all the OAuth flows are now disabled for third-party web apps and need to be manually enabled before deployment if required.

To verify that the patch is applied correctly, you must check that:
  *  The File version property of the file ./bin/Modules/WebDeployment/WebDeploymentConsole.exe matches the deployed release or later, and ensure that any earlier release is no longer used;
  *  Web Sites have been redeployed;
  *  OAuth flow are correctly set for each authorized Client.





Available patches:
Patch provided in:
  *  PcVue 16.3.4 (16.3.4902.3112)
  *  PcVue 15.2.14 (15.2.14900.37147)

supportingMedia.value:
Neo4j Enterprise and Community editions versions prior to 2026.01.3 and 5.26.21 are vulnerable to a potential information disclosure by a user who has ability to access the local log files.

The "obfuscate_literals" option in the query logs does not redact error information, exposing unredacted data in the query log when a customer writes a query that fails. It can allow a user with legitimate access to the local log files to obtain information they are not authorised to see. If this user is also in a position to run queries and trigger errors, this vulnerability can potentially help them to infer information they are not authorised to see through their intended database access.

We recommend upgrading to versions 2026.01.3 (or 5.26.21) where the issue is fixed, and reviewing query log files permissions to ensure restricted access. If your configuration had db.logs.query.obfuscate_literals enabled, and you wish the obfuscation to cover the error messages as well, you need to enable the new configuration setting db.logs.query.obfuscate_errors once you have upgraded Neo4j.

adp.title: org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants: Disabled identity providers are still accepted for JWT Authorization Grant

solutions.value: RHSA-2026:2366: Red Hat build of Keycloak 26.4
RHSA-2026:2365: Red Hat build of Keycloak 26.4.9

workarounds.value: To mitigate this issue, administrators should immediately revoke or rotate the signing keys associated with any Identity Provider that has been disabled in Keycloak. This operational control is crucial to prevent unauthorized token issuance by ensuring that compromised or offboarded IdP keys cannot be used to generate valid JWT assertions.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in Keycloak. A vulnerability exists in the jwt-authorization-grant flow where the server fails to verify if an Identity Provider (IdP) is enabled before issuing tokens. The issuer lookup mechanism (lookupIdentityProviderFromIssuer) retrieves the IdP configuration but does not filter for isEnabled=false. If an administrator disables an IdP (e.g., due to a compromise or offboarding), an entity possessing that IdP's signing key can still generate valid JWT assertions that Keycloak accepts, resulting in the issuance of valid access tokens.

descriptions.description: Improperly Implemented Security Check for Standard

adp.title: keylime: Keylime: Authentication bypass allows unauthorized administrative operations due to missing client-side TLS authentication

affected.product: Red Hat Enterprise Linux AppStream EUS (v. 10.0)

solutions.value: RHSA-2026:2298: Red Hat Enterprise Linux AppStream EUS (v. 10.0)
RHSA-2026:2225: Red Hat Enterprise Linux AppStream (v. 10)
RHSA-2026:2224: Red Hat Enterprise Linux AppStream (v. 9)

workarounds.value:
Restrict network access to the Keylime registrar's HTTPS port (default 8891) to only trusted verifier and tenant hosts using firewall rules. 
Alternatively, deploy a reverse proxy (e.g., Nginx, HAProxy) in front of the registrar to enforce client certificate authentication. 
Ensure any changes to firewall rules or proxy configurations are reloaded or services are restarted for the mitigation to take effect.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in Keylime. The Keylime registrar, since version 7.12.0, does not enforce client-side Transport Layer Security (TLS) authentication. This authentication bypass vulnerability allows unauthenticated clients with network access to perform administrative operations, including listing agents, retrieving public Trusted Platform Module (TPM) data, and deleting agents, by connecting without presenting a client certificate.

descriptions.value:
n8n contains a critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in its workflow Expression evaluation system. Expressions supplied by authenticated users during workflow configuration may be evaluated in an execution context that is not sufficiently isolated from the underlying runtime.

descriptions.value: Jirafeau normally prevents browser preview for text files due to the possibility that for example SVG and HTML documents could be exploited for cross site scripting. This was done by storing the MIME type of a file and allowing only browser preview for MIME types beginning with image (except for image/svg+xml, see CVE-2022-30110, CVE-2024-12326 and CVE-2025-7066), video and audio. However, it was possible to bypass this check by sending a manipulated HTTP request with an invalid MIME type like image. When doing the preview, the browser tries to automatically detect the MIME type resulting in detecting SVG and possibly executing JavaScript code. To prevent this, MIME sniffing is disabled by sending the HTTP header X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

cna.title: dns: memory‑safety issue in the DNS name parser

descriptions.value: dns_unpack_name() caches the buffer tailroom once and reuses it while appending DNS labels. As the buffer grows, the cached size becomes incorrect, and the final null terminator can be written past the buffer. With assertions disabled (default), a malicious DNS response can trigger an out-of-bounds write when CONFIG_DNS_RESOLVER is enabled.

cna.title: Incorrect management of session invalidation vulnerability in Graylog Web Interface

solutions.value: It is recommended to update the software to the latest version, where the vulnerability described has already been mitigated. For the affected version, the vulnerability is not mitigated, as the manufacturer considers all versions prior to the current one to be obsolete.

supportingMedia.value: It is recommended to update the software to the latest version, where the vulnerability described has already been mitigated. For the affected version, the vulnerability is not mitigated, as the manufacturer considers all versions prior to the current one to be obsolete.

descriptions.value: Not properly invalidated session vulnerability in Graylog Web Interface, version 2.2.3, due to incorrect management of session invalidation after new logins. The application generates a new 'sessionId' each time a user authenticates, but does not invalidate previously issued session identifiers, which remain valid even after multiple consecutive logins by the same user. As a result, a stolen or leaked 'sessionId' can continue to be used to authenticate valid requests. Exploiting this vulnerability would allow an attacker with access to the web service/API network (port 9000 or HTTP/S endpoint of the server) to reuse an old session token to gain unauthorized access to the application, interact with the API/web, and compromise the integrity of the affected account.

The EnerVista URPC installation software versions prior to 8.70, used an incorrect method of 
loading the DLL (dynamic Link Library) file by referencing it relative to the location of the installation 
folder. If the system in which the software is installed gets compromised, an attacker could exploit 
this weakness and replace the legitimate DLL with a malicious file. 


The EnerVista UR Setup software installation has been upgraded to address this vulnerability.

It is essential for organizations to prioritize cybersecurity measures, including regular vulnerability 
assessments and prompt application of security patches.

cna.title: Arbitrary Code Execution via Unsafe torch.load() in Trainer Checkpoint Loading in huggingface/transformers

descriptions.value: A vulnerability in the HuggingFace Transformers library, specifically in the `Trainer` class, allows for arbitrary code execution. The `_load_rng_state()` method in `src/transformers/trainer.py` at line 3059 calls `torch.load()` without the `weights_only=True` parameter. This issue affects all versions of the library supporting `torch>=2.2` when used with PyTorch versions below 2.6, as the `safe_globals()` context manager provides no protection in these versions. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by supplying a malicious checkpoint file, such as `rng_state.pth`, which can execute arbitrary code when loaded. The issue is resolved in version v5.0.0rc3.

descriptions.value: In the Eclipse OMR port library component since release 0.2.0, an API function to return the textual names of all supported processor features was not accounting for the separator inserted between processor features. Tokens issued to a low-privileged user are not sufficiently restricted, allowing them to be used to access product-level Admin REST APIs.

descriptions.value: The Tutor LMS – eLearning and online course solution plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR) in all versions up to, and including, 3.9.5. workarounds.value: To mitigate this issue, disable DNSSEC validation on affected BIND resolvers. Alternatively, configure the BIND server as authoritative-only if recursive queries are not required. Disabling DNSSEC validation may reduce the security posture of the DNS resolver. A restart of the BIND service (`named`) is required for these changes to take effect and may temporarily interrupt DNS resolution.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in BIND. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a maliciously crafted DNSSEC-validated zone to a BIND resolver. This could cause the resolver to consume excessive CPU resources, leading to a denial of service (DoS) for legitimate users.

credits.value: ISC would like to thank Samy Medjahed/Ap4sh for bringing this vulnerability to our attention.

descriptions.value: If this issue is encountered, the resolver may experience excessive CPU consumption and a sharp decrease in the number of queries per second that it can handle.

exploits.value: We are not aware of any active exploits.

solutions.value: Upgrade to the patched release most closely related to your current version of BIND 9: 9.18.47, 9.20.21, 9.21.20, 9.18.47-S1, or 9.20.21-S1.

workarounds.value: This is not recommended, but disabling DNSSEC (`dnssec-validation no;`) prevents exploitation of this issue.

descriptions.value:
If a BIND resolver is performing DNSSEC validation and encounters a maliciously crafted zone, the resolver may consume excessive CPU. Authoritative-only servers are generally unaffected, although there are circumstances where authoritative servers may make recursive queries (see: https://kb.isc.org/docs/why-does-my-authoritative-server-make-recursive-queries).
This issue affects BIND 9 versions 9.11.0 through 9.16.50, 9.18.0 through 9.18.46, 9.20.0 through 9.20.20, 9.21.0 through 9.21.19, 9.11.3-S1 through 9.16.50-S1, 9.18.11-S1 through 9.18.46-S1, and 9.20.9-S1 through 9.20.20-S1.

cna.title: Loco Translate <= 2.8.2 - Authenticated (Translator+) Path Traversal to Limited File Read via 'ref' Parameter

descriptions.value: The Loco Translate plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Path Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.2 via the `fsReference` AJAX route. This is due to the `findSourceFile()` method normalizing user-supplied `ref` paths containing `../` directory traversal sequences without validating that the resolved path remains within the intended bundle or content directory. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Translator-level access and above (custom `loco_admin` capability required, granted to the `translator` role and administrators by default), to read arbitrary `.php`, `.js`, `.json`, and `.twig` files from the server filesystem outside the intended translation directory. Files named wp-config.php are excluded.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in undici. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted WebSocket frame with an extremely large 64-bit length. This causes undici's ByteParser to overflow its internal calculations, leading to an invalid state and a fatal TypeError. The primary consequence is a Denial of Service (DoS), which terminates the process.

solutions.value:
PX4 recommends enabling MAVLink 2.0 message signing as the 
authentication mechanism for all non‑USB communication links. PX4 has 
published a security hardening guide for integrators and manufacturers 
at

Message signing configuration documentation can be found at 
https://docs.px4.io/main/en/mavlink/message_signing

descriptions.value:
The MAVLink communication protocol does not require cryptographic 
authentication by default. When MAVLink 2.0 message signing is not 
enabled, any message -- including SERIAL_CONTROL, which provides 
interactive shell access -- can be sent by an unauthenticated party with
 access to the MAVLink interface. PX4 provides MAVLink 2.0 message 
signing as the cryptographic authentication mechanism for all MAVLink 
communication. When signing is enabled, unsigned messages are rejected 
at the protocol level.

descriptions.value: Rapid7 Nexpose versions 6.4.50 and later are vulnerable to an insufficient entropy issue in the CredentialsKeyStorePassword.generateRandomPassword() method. solutions.value:
Harden the configuration
Who should apply this recommendation: All users


To reduce the risk of exploitation, ARC Informatique strongly recommends implementing the following defensive measures:

  *  Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, and ensure they are not accessible from insecure networks.
  *  Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolate them from business networks.
  *  When remote access is required, use secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as its connected devices.



Uninstall the Web Server 
Who should apply this recommendation: All users not using the affected component 

If your system does not require the use of the Web & Mobile features, you should make sure not to install them. If your system requires the use of the Web & Mobile features, they should be installed only on the Web Server.
See the product help related to the installation for more information.




Update IIS configuration – manually update HTTP headers
Who should apply this recommendation: 

All users running affected components.



As a quick mitigation for the unnecessary and missing HTTP headers, you can disable default headers and add secure HTTP headers for all requests. Those options can be set via the web.config file located on the IIS by following those steps:
  *  Open the file C:\inetpub\<SV Website>\web.config
  *  Add the following entries to the section customHeaders, which are the recommendations from the official OWASP site:
<remove name="X-Powered-By" />
<add name="X-Frame-Options" value="DENY" />
<add name="X-XSS-Protection" value="0" />
<add name="X-Content-Type-Options" value="nosniff" />
<add name="X-DNS-Prefetch-Control" value="off" />
<add name="Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy" value="same-origin" />
<add name="Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy" value="require-corp" />
<add name="Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy" value="same-site" />
<add name="Referrer-Policy" value="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" />
<add name="Strict-Transport-Security" value="max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload" />
<add name="Permissions-Policy" value="geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()" />


Update the Web Deployment Console (WDC) and re deploy the Web Server
Who should apply this recommendation: 

All users running affected components.



Install a patched release of the Web Deployment Console (WDC) on the IIS Web server and use it to re-deploy the Web Site. Some settings might need to be updated if third-party web apps or services depend on the OAuth ROPC flow.

In a patched release of the WDC, new settings are available for each authorized Client to enable or disable:
  *  The Authorization Code flow
  *  The Authorization Code flow with PKCE
  *  The Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC) flow


By default, all the OAuth flows are now disabled for third-party web apps and need to be manually enabled before deployment if required.

To verify that the patch is applied correctly, you must check that:
  *  The File version property of the file ./bin/Modules/WebDeployment/WebDeploymentConsole.exe matches the deployed release or later, and ensure that any earlier release is no longer used;
  *  Web Sites have been redeployed;
  *  OAuth flow are correctly set for each authorized Client.







Available patches:
Patch provided in:
  *  PcVue 16.3.4 (16.3.4902.3112)
  *  PcVue 15.2.14 (15.2.14900.37147)

Update the Web Deployment Console (WDC) and re deploy the Web Server
Who should apply this recommendation: All users running affected components.

Install a patched release of the Web Deployment Console (WDC) on the IIS Web server and use it to re-deploy the Web Site. Some settings might need to be updated if third-party web apps or services depend on the OAuth ROPC flow.

In a patched release of the WDC, new settings are available for each authorized Client to enable or disable:
  • The Authorization Code flow
  • The Authorization Code flow with PKCE
  • The Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC) flow
By default, all the OAuth flows are now disabled for third-party web apps and need to be manually enabled before deployment if required.

To verify that the patch is applied correctly, you must check that:
  • The File version property of the file ./bin/Modules/WebDeployment/WebDeploymentConsole.exe matches the deployed release or later, and ensure that any earlier release is no longer used;
  • Web Sites have been redeployed;
  • OAuth flow are correctly set for each authorized Client.

solutions.value:
Harden the configuration
Who should apply this recommendation: All users


To reduce the risk of exploitation, ARC Informatique strongly recommends implementing the following defensive measures:

  *  Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, and ensure they are not accessible from insecure networks.
  *  Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolate them from business networks.
  *  When remote access is required, use secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as its connected devices.



Uninstall the Web Server 
Who should apply this recommendation: All users not using the affected component 

If your system does not require the use of the Web & Mobile features, you should make sure not to install them. If your system requires the use of the Web & Mobile features, they should be installed only on the Web Server.
See the product help related to the installation for more information.


Update the Web Deployment Console (WDC) and re deploy the Web Server
Who should apply this recommendation: 

All users running affected components.



Install a patched release of the Web Deployment Console (WDC) on the IIS Web server and use it to re-deploy the Web Site. Some settings might need to be updated if third-party web apps or services depend on the OAuth ROPC flow.

In a patched release of the WDC, new settings are available for each authorized Client to enable or disable:
  *  The Authorization Code flow
  *  The Authorization Code flow with PKCE
  *  The Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC) flow


By default, all the OAuth flows are now disabled for third-party web apps and need to be manually enabled before deployment if required.

To verify that the patch is applied correctly, you must check that:
  *  The File version property of the file ./bin/Modules/WebDeployment/WebDeploymentConsole.exe matches the deployed release or later, and ensure that any earlier release is no longer used;
  *  Web Sites have been redeployed;
  *  OAuth flow are correctly set for each authorized Client.





Available patches:
Patch provided in:
  *  PcVue 16.3.4 (16.3.4902.3112)
  *  PcVue 15.2.14 (15.2.14900.37147)

descriptions.value: The Livemesh Addons for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 9.0. This is due to insufficient sanitization of the template name parameter in the `lae_get_template_part()` function, which uses an inadequate `str_replace()` approach that can be bypassed using recursive directory traversal patterns. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to include and execute arbitrary files on the server, allowing the attacker to include and execute local files via the widget's template parameter granted they can trick an administrator into performing an action or install Elementor.

cna.title: Membership Plugin – Restrict Content <= 3.2.20 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via 'rcp_level'

descriptions.value: The Membership Plugin – Restrict Content plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 3.2.20. This is due to the `rcp_setup_registration_init()` function accepting any membership level ID via the `rcp_level` POST parameter without validating that the level is active or that payment is required. Combined with the `add_user_role()` method which assigns the WordPress role configured on the membership level without status checks, this makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to register with any membership level, including inactive levels that grant privileged WordPress roles such as Administrator, or paid levels that charge a sign-up fee. The vulnerability was partially patched in version 3.2.18.

This is due to the plugin containing hardcoded MySQL database credentials for the vendor's external telemetry server in the `Mementor_TTS_Remote_Telemetry` class. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract and decode these credentials, gaining unauthorized write access to the vendor's telemetry database.

cna.title: Altium 365 Over-Permissive CORS Configuration Allows Credentialed Cross-Origin Workspace Access

descriptions.value: CAPEC-122 Privilege Abuse
CAPEC-17 Accessing, Modifying, or Executing Executable Files
CAPEC-233 Privilege Escalation via Trust Boundary Violation

Altium 365 workspace endpoints were configured with an overly permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policy that allowed credentialed cross-origin requests from other Altium-controlled subdomains, including forum.live.altium.com. As a result, JavaScript executing on those origins could access authenticated workspace APIs in the context of a logged-in user. When chained with vulnerabilities in those external applications, this misconfiguration enables unauthorized access to workspace data, administrative actions, and bypass of IP allowlisting controls, including in GovCloud environments.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the jsonpath component. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to achieve arbitrary code execution by supplying a malicious JSON Path expression. The component's reliance on the `static-eval` module for processing user-supplied input leads to unsafe evaluation. Successful exploitation can result in Remote Code Execution (RCE) in Node.js environments or Cross-site Scripting (XSS) in browser contexts.

descriptions.description: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

descriptions.value: Versions of the package jsonpath before 1.3.0 are vulnerable to Arbitrary Code Injection via unsafe evaluation of user-supplied JSON Path expressions. The library relies on the static-eval module to process JSON Path input, which is not designed to handle untrusted data safely. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by supplying a malicious JSON Path expression that, when evaluated, executes arbitrary JavaScript code, leading to Remote Code Execution in Node.js environments or Cross-site Scripting (XSS) in browser contexts. This affects all methods that evaluate JSON Paths against objects, including .query, .nodes, .paths, .value, .parent, and .apply.

solutions.value:
Harden the configuration
Who should apply this recommendation: All users


To reduce the risk of exploitation, ARC Informatique strongly recommends implementing the following defensive measures:

  *  Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, and ensure they are not accessible from insecure networks.
  *  Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolate them from business networks.
  *  When remote access is required, use secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as its connected devices.



Uninstall the Web Server 
Who should apply this recommendation: All users not using the affected component 

If your system does not require the use of the Web & Mobile features, you should make sure not to install them. If your system requires the use of the Web & Mobile features, they should be installed only on the Web Server.
See the product help related to the installation for more information.


Update the Web Deployment Console (WDC) and re deploy the Web Server
Who should apply this recommendation: 

All users running affected components.



Install a patched release of the Web Deployment Console (WDC) on the IIS Web server and use it to re-deploy the Web Site. Some settings might need to be updated if third-party web apps or services depend on the OAuth ROPC flow.

In a patched release of the WDC, new settings are available for each authorized Client to enable or disable:
  *  The Authorization Code flow
  *  The Authorization Code flow with PKCE
  *  The Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC) flow


By default, all the OAuth flows are now disabled for third-party web apps and need to be manually enabled before deployment if required.

To verify that the patch is applied correctly, you must check that:
  *  The File version property of the file ./bin/Modules/WebDeployment/WebDeploymentConsole.exe matches the deployed release or later, and ensure that any earlier release is no longer used;
  *  Web Sites have been redeployed;
  *  OAuth flow are correctly set for each authorized Client.





Available patches:
Patch provided in:
  *  PcVue 16.3.4 (16.3.4902.3112)
  *  PcVue 15.2.14 (15.2.14900.37147)
